title: Design System: Camilo Parra — The Dark Hour

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The only easing. Blade glide 500ms, colour 300ms, section wipe 900ms.

components.name: Blade Menu
components.description: Pause-menu commands with a mono sub-label naming each section plainly; the cyan blade rests on the active item and slides to hover.
components.css: .ds-menu { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 16px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-start; gap: 4px; background: #161d2c; transform: rotate(-6deg); } .ds-menu a { display: block; padding: 0.2em 0.7em; font: italic 800 40px/0.86 'Barlow Condensed', sans-serif; text-transform: uppercase; color: #cdd5e3; text-decoration: none; transition: color 0.3s, background 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); clip-path: polygon(0.6em 0, 100% 0, calc(100% - 0.6em) 100%, 0 100%); } .ds-menu a.on, .ds-menu a:hover, .ds-menu a:focus-visible { background: #74bfe3; color: #161d2c; outline: none; }

narrative.overview: The portfolio lives in the hidden hour after midnight. A WebGL ordered-dither moon and sea fill the background, a slanted pause menu sits in front of it, and every section is a menu command stamped with its own minute. Dithering is the one image language; type is loud, tilted and condensed against dense mono readouts.
keyCharacteristics: One cyan on midnight blue; Day mode is the same kit worn away.
Parallelogram "blades" for selection and buttons; no rounded corners anywhere.
Every image is dithered or ASCII; the background is a live shader.
Every jargon label is paired with a plain mono sub-label.

rules.name: The Home/Away Kit Rule
rules.body: Themes are value swaps on the same tokens. Never add a colour that exists in one theme only.

rules.name: The One Cyan Rule
rules.body: Cyan is the only hue. Status, success and emphasis all use cyan or ink.

rules.name: The Scrim Rule
rules.body: Body copy that sits over the dither sea gets a ground-coloured scrim so particles never drop contrast below AA.

rules.name: The Tilt Rule
rules.body: Display type is rotated -6° from its left origin. Body and mono copy never tilt.

rules.name: The Headroom Rule
rules.body: At line-height 0.86, accents rise above the line box. Never clip display text to its exact box.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Separation comes from scrims, tone and tilt. A drop shadow would contradict the flat dither print.

dos: Do put every image through the dither or ASCII pipeline, including real photos when they arrive.
Do give each new section a minute between 00:00 and 01:00 and a tilted headline.
Do use the blade cut for any new selectable or pressable surface.
Do put a ground scrim behind any copy placed over the sea.
Do mark missing owner content with .pending and say so in the copy, both languages.
donts: Don't introduce rounded corners, drop shadows or a second accent hue.
Don't use Atlus or Persona logos, characters, fonts or names. Borrow the grammar only.
Don't clip display type to its exact line box; accents need headroom.
Don't invent testimonials, employers, dates or metrics to fill a pending slot.
